The Earth–Large Magellanic Cloud distance is approximately \(160{,}000\) light-years.

For \(v=0.99999987c\), the Lorentz factor is

\[
\gamma=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}}
      =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(0.99999987)^2}}
      \approx 1961.
\]

The astronaut experiences time dilation, so the proper travel time is approximately

\[
t_{\text{astronaut}}
=\frac{160{,}000\ \text{years}}{1961}
\approx 81.6\ \text{years}.
\]

Thus, the astronaut would be about \(22+82=104\) years old upon arrival, below the average lifetime of 150 years. The closest option is 81 years.

Answer: A
